115:     "platform. Write the next message the assistant sends to the user. "
116:     "Answer in the conversation's language. One to three short sentences, plain "
117:     "text: no markdown, no emoji, no letter salutation and no signature. "
118:     "If a question is given, ask it naturally in your own words. "
119:     "Never invent a listing, a price or a fact that is not in the context, and "
120:     "never promise anything the platform did not confirm."
121: )
122: 
123: # A short, provider-neutral gloss for each question, so the reply model knows
124: # what it is asking for without reading the outbound layer's copy.
125: QUESTION_TOPICS: dict[str, str] = {
126:     "ask.property_type": "the type of property (apartment, studio, house, ...)",
127:     "ask.standing": "whether the property is modern or not",
128:     "ask.location": "the city and neighbourhood",
129:     "ask.rent": "the monthly rent, in XAF",
130:     "ask.features": "the number of bedrooms and bathrooms, and the surface in m2",
131:     "ask.charges": "whether charges are included and, if not, their monthly amount",
132:     "ask.minimum_duration": "the minimum rental duration",
133:     "ask.availability": "whether the property is still available",
134:     "ask.conditions": "the tenant conditions (deposit, duration, tenant type)",
135:     "ask.confirm_property": "confirmation of the summary before publishing",
136:     "confirm.published": "confirmation that the property has been published",
137: }
138: 
139: # What a month of rent costs here, by property type, in XAF. A model with no
140: # Cameroonian grounding reads a bare "50" as fifty francs; these wide bands anchor
141: # the magnitude only — they never reject a price the user is sure about.
142: PRICE_REFERENCES_XAF: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {
143:     "ROOM": (10_000, 60_000),
144:     "STUDIO": (20_000, 150_000),
145:     "APARTMENT": (40_000, 400_000),
146:     "HOUSE": (80_000, 800_000),
147:     "DUPLEX": (150_000, 1_500_000),
148: }
149: 
150: # The same question is asked from opposite sides: a landlord lists a property, a
151: # tenant looks for one. The neutral gloss lets the model default to the tenant
152: # reading ("le loyer que vous recherchez") even in a listing, which reads as if
153: # the platform had mixed the two roles up. These overlays fix the wording.
154: _LANDLORD_TOPICS: dict[str, str] = {
155:     "ask.property_type": "the type of property the landlord is listing",
156:     "ask.standing": "whether the property the landlord is listing is modern or not",
157:     "ask.location": "the city and neighbourhood where the property is",
158:     "ask.rent": "the monthly rent the landlord is asking, in XAF",
159: }
160: _TENANT_TOPICS: dict[str, str] = {
161:     "ask.property_type": "the type of property the tenant is looking for",
162:     "ask.standing": "whether the tenant wants a modern property or not",
163:     "ask.location": "the city and neighbourhood the tenant wants",
164:     "ask.rent": "the maximum monthly rent the tenant is willing to pay, in XAF",
165: }
166: _FLOW_TOPICS: dict[FlowName, dict[str, str]] = {
167:     FlowName.PROPERTY_CREATION: _LANDLORD_TOPICS,
168:     FlowName.PROPERTY_SEARCH: _TENANT_TOPICS,
169: }
170: _FLOW_ROLES: dict[FlowName, str] = {
171:     FlowName.PROPERTY_CREATION: "a landlord listing a property for rent",
172:     FlowName.PROPERTY_SEARCH: "a tenant looking for a property to rent",
173:     FlowName.SUPPORT: "a user who needs help with the platform",
174: }
175: 
176: 
177: def question_topic(next_key: str | None, flow: FlowName) -> str | None:
178:     """The plain-words gloss of the next question, phrased for this flow."""
179:     if not next_key:
180:         return None
181:     overlay = _FLOW_TOPICS.get(flow, {})
182:     return overlay.get(next_key) or QUESTION_TOPICS.get(next_key)
183: 
184: RESPONSE_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
185:     "type": "object",
186:     "required": ["intent", "confidence", "entities"],
187:     "properties": {
188:         "intent": {"type": "string", "enum": list(ALLOWED_INTENTS)},
189:         "confidence": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1},
190:         "language": {"type": "string"},
191:         "reply": {"type": "string"},
192:         "entities": {
193:             "type": "object",
194:             "properties": {
195:                 "property_type": {"type": "string"},
196:                 "standing": {"type": "string", "enum": ["MODERN", "NON_MODERN"]},
197:                 "city": {"type": "string"},
198:                 "neighbourhood": {"type": "string"},
199:                 "price": {"type": "integer"},
200:                 "bedrooms": {"type": "integer"},
201:                 "bathrooms": {"type": "integer"},
202:                 "surface_area": {"type": "integer"},
203:             },
204:         },
205:     },
206: }

244: class AnalyseConversationMessageUseCase:
245:     name = USE_CASE
246: 
247:     def __init__(
248:         self,
249:         uow: UnitOfWork,
250:         *,
251:         inbound: InboundMessageRepository,
252:         sessions: ConversationSessionRepository,
253:         turns: ConversationTurnRepository,
254:         usage: AiUsageLedger,
255:         classifier: DeterministicClassifier | None = None,
256:         model: IntentModel | None = None,
257:         response_model: ResponseModel | None = None,
258:         extractor: FactExtractor | None = None,
259:         budget: BudgetPolicy | None = None,
260:         provider_name: str = "openrouter",
261:         listing: PropertyListing | None = None,
262:     ) -> None:
263:         self._uow = uow
264:         self._inbound = inbound
265:         self._sessions = sessions
266:         self._turns = turns
267:         self._usage = usage
268:         self._classifier = classifier or DeterministicClassifier()
269:         self._model = model
270:         self._response_model = response_model
271:         self._extractor = extractor or FactExtractor()
272:         self._budget = budget
273:         self._provider = provider_name
274:         self._listing = listing
275: 
276:     async def execute(self, command: AnalysisCommand, *, now: datetime) -> AnalysisReport:
277:         moment = ensure_utc(now)
278: 
279:         message = await self._inbound.get_by_id(command.message_id)
280:         session = (
281:             await self._sessions.get_by_id(command.session_id) if message is not None else None
282:         )
283:         if message is None or session is None:
284:             # Nothing was written yet, and inventing a session would be worse
285:             # than admitting the message is gone.
286:             return AnalysisReport(
287:                 session_id=command.session_id,
288:                 message_id=command.message_id,
289:                 intent="UNKNOWN",
290:                 confidence=0.0,
291:                 used_llm=False,
292:                 accepted=False,
293:                 reason="message_not_found" if message is None else "session_not_found",
294:             )
295: 
296:         history = await self._turns.recent(session.id, limit=5)
297: 
298:         # Nothing has been written yet, so releasing the transaction costs
299:         # nothing and the model call never holds a database connection.
300:         await self._uow.commit()
301: 
302:         text = message.text or ""
303:         pending = session.context.get("next_question")
304:         pending_key = pending if isinstance(pending, str) else None
305: 
306:         if self._model is None:
307:             return await self._without_a_model(
308:                 session,
309:                 message_id=command.message_id,
310:                 text=text,
311:                 pending=pending_key,
312:                 now=moment,
313:             )
314: 
315:         # The rules are a fast lane now, not the primary reader: only replies a
316:         # model could not improve ("oui", "250 000 fcfa") skip the call. The open
317:         # question is passed along so a bare "non" answers "moderne ou non"
318:         # instead of being read as a refusal.
319:         shortcut = self._classifier.shortcut(text, pending=pending_key)
320:         if shortcut is not None:
321:             ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="regex").inc()
322:             return await self._finish(
323:                 session=session,
324:                 message_id=command.message_id,
325:                 intent=shortcut.intent,
326:                 confidence=shortcut.confidence,
327:                 entities=dict(shortcut.entities),
328:                 used_llm=False,
329:                 latency_ms=0,
330:                 cost_usd=Decimal("0"),
331:                 now=moment,
332:             )
333: 
334:         decision = await self._budget_decision(session.user_id, moment)
335:         if not decision.allowed:
336:             ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="budget").inc()
337:             return await self._finish(
338:                 session=session,
339:                 message_id=command.message_id,
340:                 intent="UNKNOWN",
341:                 confidence=0.0,
342:                 entities={},
343:                 used_llm=False,
344:                 latency_ms=0,
345:                 cost_usd=Decimal("0"),
346:                 now=moment,
347:                 reason=decision.reason,
348:             )
349: 
350:         ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="llm").inc()
351:         prompt = build_analysis_prompt(
352:             text=message.text,
353:             language=session.language,
354:             history=history,
355:             flow=session.flow,
356:             step=session.step,
357:             pending_question=pending_key,
358:             known_facts=dict(session.context),
359:         )
360:         result = await self._model.understand_intent(prompt)
361:         entities = dict(result.entities)
362:         # The locale shorthand ("50 mil") is a rule, not a guess: when the
363:         # message spells one it overrides whatever number the model proposed,
364:         # because the model's prior reads "mil" as a million.
365:         shorthand = self._classifier.shorthand_amount(text)
366:         if shorthand is not None:
367:             entities["price"] = shorthand
368:         verdict = self._verdict(
369:             session=session,
370:             intent=result.intent,
371:             confidence=result.confidence,
372:             entities=entities,
373:             reason=None,
374:         )
375: 
376:         # The reply is written before the write transaction opens: an LLM call
377:         # must never hold a database connection, and a reply that fails degrades
378:         # to a template rather than to silence.
379: 
380:         # Preferred path: the classification call already wrote the reply in its
381:         # JSON, so the whole turn costs one round-trip. Only a model that left
382:         # ``reply`` empty pays for a second call; a deployment that never asks
383:         # for an inline reply degrades to the same behaviour as before.
384:         reply_text: str | None = result.reply
385:         reply_usage: LlmUsage | None = None
386:         if reply_text is None:
387:             reply_text, reply_usage = await self._compose_reply(
388:                 verdict=verdict,
389:                 text=text,
390:                 session=session,
391:                 history=history,
392:                 now=moment,
393:             )
394: 
395:         # Both calls are one turn: the ledger records their sum, so reply traffic
396:         # cannot spend past a budget that only counted intent calls.
397:         call_usage = result.usage
398:         model_name = call_usage.model if call_usage is not None else self._model.model
399:         input_tokens = call_usage.input_tokens if call_usage is not None else 0
400:         output_tokens = call_usage.output_tokens if call_usage is not None else 0
401:         latency_ms = call_usage.latency_ms if call_usage is not None else 0
402:         cost_usd = (
403:             Decimal(str(call_usage.estimated_cost_usd))
404:             if call_usage is not None
405:             else Decimal("0")
406:         )
407:         if reply_usage is not None:
408:             input_tokens += reply_usage.input_tokens
409:             output_tokens += reply_usage.output_tokens
410:             latency_ms += reply_usage.latency_ms
411:             cost_usd += Decimal(str(reply_usage.estimated_cost_usd))
412: 
413:         llm_calls_total.labels(use_case=USE_CASE, model=model_name, outcome="ok").inc()
414:         llm_tokens_total.labels(model=model_name, direction="input").inc(input_tokens)
415:         llm_tokens_total.labels(model=model_name, direction="output").inc(output_tokens)
416:         llm_latency_seconds.labels(use_case=USE_CASE, model=model_name).observe(
417:             latency_ms / 1000
418:         )
419:         if cost_usd > 0:
420:             llm_cost_usd_total.labels(use_case=USE_CASE).inc(float(cost_usd))
421: 
422:         return await self._apply(
423:             session=session,
424:             message_id=command.message_id,
425:             verdict=verdict,
426:             confidence=result.confidence,
427:             used_llm=True,
428:             latency_ms=latency_ms,
429:             cost_usd=cost_usd,
430:             now=moment,
431:             model_name=model_name,
432:             input_tokens=input_tokens,
433:             output_tokens=output_tokens,
434:             reply_text=reply_text,
435:         )
436: 
437:     async def _without_a_model(
438:         self,
439:         session: ConversationSession,
440:         *,
441:         message_id: uuid.UUID,
442:         text: str,
443:         pending: str | None,
444:         now: datetime,
445:     ) -> AnalysisReport:
446:         """The deployment has no AI key: fall back to regexes and templates.
447: 
448:         The rule set here is the full classifier, not the fast lane, because it
449:         is now the only reader. An unresolved message still records its turn and
450:         asks the user to rephrase instead of leaving the thread silent.
451:         """
452:         match = self._classifier.classify(text, pending=pending)
453:         if match is not None:
454:             ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="regex").inc()
455:             return await self._finish(
456:                 session=session,
457:                 message_id=message_id,
458:                 intent=match.intent,
459:                 confidence=match.confidence,
460:                 entities=dict(match.entities),
461:                 used_llm=False,
462:                 latency_ms=0,
463:                 cost_usd=Decimal("0"),
464:                 now=now,
465:             )
466:         ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="budget").inc()
467:         return await self._finish(
468:             session=session,
469:             message_id=message_id,
470:             intent="UNKNOWN",
471:             confidence=0.0,
472:             entities={},
473:             used_llm=False,
474:             latency_ms=0,
475:             cost_usd=Decimal("0"),
476:             now=now,
477:             reason="no_model_configured",
478:         )
479: 
480:     async def _finish(
481:         self,
482:         *,
483:         session: ConversationSession,
484:         message_id: uuid.UUID,
485:         intent: str,
486:         confidence: float,
487:         entities: dict[str, Any],
488:         used_llm: bool,
489:         latency_ms: int,
490:         cost_usd: Decimal,
491:         now: datetime,
492:         reason: str | None = None,
493:     ) -> AnalysisReport:
494:         """Close a call that did not reach the model: no reply is written."""
495:         return await self._apply(
496:             session=session,
497:             message_id=message_id,
498:             verdict=self._verdict(
499:                 session=session,
500:                 intent=intent,
501:                 confidence=confidence,
502:                 entities=entities,
503:                 reason=reason,
504:             ),
505:             confidence=confidence,
506:             used_llm=used_llm,
507:             latency_ms=latency_ms,
508:             cost_usd=cost_usd,
509:             now=now,
510:         )
511: 
512:     def _verdict(
513:         self,
514:         *,
515:         session: ConversationSession,
516:         intent: str,
517:         confidence: float,
518:         entities: dict[str, Any],
519:         reason: str | None,
520:     ) -> _Verdict:
521:         """Validate a proposal through the domain, before anything is written.
522: 
523:         Split out of ``_apply`` so the reply can be written from the *outcome*
524:         of the turn — the next question, or the fact it was refused — while the
525:         write transaction is still closed.
526:         """
527:         if not is_supported_intent(intent):
528:             intent, reason = "UNKNOWN", reason or "unsupported_intent"
529:         if reason is None and confidence < MIN_ACCEPTED_CONFIDENCE:
530:             reason = "low_confidence"
531: 
532:         facts = self._extractor.validate(entities)
533:         # The next step must consider the whole form, not just this message: a
534:         # landlord who gives their city after naming the property type is one
535:         # step further, not back at the type question. When this message opens a
536:         # *new* flow, the old facts belong to the abandoned attempt and are
537:         # deliberately ignored — matching the reset ``_advance_session`` does.
538:         opening_flow = FLOW_BY_OPENING_INTENT.get(intent)
539:         starts_new_flow = opening_flow is not None and session.flow is not opening_flow
540:         known = {} if starts_new_flow else dict(session.context)
541:         next_step = (
542:             self._extractor.next_step(intent, facts, flow=session.flow, known=known)
543:             if reason is None
544:             else None
545:         )
546:         return _Verdict(
547:             intent=intent,
548:             facts=facts,
549:             accepted=reason is None,
550:             reason=reason,
551:             next_step=next_step,
552:         )
553: 
554:     async def _compose_reply(
555:         self,
556:         *,
557:         verdict: _Verdict,
558:         text: str,
559:         session: ConversationSession,
560:         history: list[TurnSummary],
561:         now: datetime,
562:     ) -> tuple[str | None, LlmUsage | None]:
563:         """Let the model phrase the answer, or return ``(None, None)``.
564: 
565:         ``None`` means "use the template": either no response model is
566:         configured, or writing it failed. A reply failure must never cost the
567:         user their turn, so the exception is swallowed here and the outbound
568:         layer falls back to its stable copy.
569:         """
570:         if self._response_model is None or not text.strip():
571:             return None, None
572: 
573:         next_key = question_key_for(verdict.next_step) if verdict.accepted else None
574:         prompt = build_reply_prompt(
575:             text=text,
576:             language=session.language,
577:             verdict=verdict,
578:             next_key=next_key,
579:             history=history,
580:             flow=session.flow,
581:         )
582:         try:
583:             response = await self._response_model.generate_response(prompt)
584:         except DomainError:
585:             return None, None
586:         sentence = response.content.strip()
587:         if not sentence:
588:             return None, None
589:         return sentence, response.usage
590: 
591:     async def _apply(
592:         self,
593:         *,
594:         session: ConversationSession,
595:         message_id: uuid.UUID,
596:         verdict: _Verdict,
597:         confidence: float,
598:         used_llm: bool,
599:         latency_ms: int,
600:         cost_usd: Decimal,
601:         now: datetime,
602:         model_name: str | None = None,
603:         input_tokens: int = 0,
604:         output_tokens: int = 0,
605:         reply_text: str | None = None,
606:     ) -> AnalysisReport:
607:         """Record the turn, move the conversation, and stage the answer.
608: 
609:         Extraction already happened in ``_verdict``; a rejected outcome is still
610:         recorded, so "the model was unsure" stays measurable instead of being
611:         silently converted into a wrong listing.
612:         """
613:         intent = verdict.intent
614:         facts = verdict.facts
615:         next_step = verdict.next_step
616:         reason = verdict.reason
617:         accepted = verdict.accepted
618: 
619:         await self._turns.add(
620:             ConversationTurn(
621:                 session_id=session.id,
622:                 message_id=message_id,
623:                 direction="INBOUND",
624:                 intent=intent,
625:                 confidence=confidence,
626:                 used_llm=used_llm,
627:                 latency_ms=latency_ms,
628:                 occurred_at=now,
629:             )
630:         )
631:         if used_llm:
632:             await self._usage.append(
633:                 UsageEntry(
634:                     use_case=USE_CASE,
635:                     provider=self._provider,
636:                     model=model_name or "unknown",
637:                     input_tokens=input_tokens,
638:                     output_tokens=output_tokens,
639:                     latency_ms=latency_ms,
640:                     cost_usd=cost_usd,
641:                     user_id=session.user_id,
642:                     conversation_id=session.id,
643:                     correlation_id=None,
644:                     occurred_at=now,
645:                 )
646:             )
647: 
648:         if accepted:
649:             listing_text, next_step, listing_id = await self._confirm_listing(
650:                 session, intent=intent, next_step=next_step, now=now
651:             )
652:             await self._advance_session(
653:                 session, intent, facts, next_step, now=now, attach_property_id=listing_id
654:             )
655:             reply_text = listing_text or reply_text
656: 
657:         # Committed with the turn: an analysis the platform understood but never
658:         # answered is a landlord staring at a silent thread, and no retry can
659:         # notice a reply that was never staged.
660:         question = question_key_for(next_step) if accepted else None
661:         await self._stage_reply(
662:             session,
663:             intent=intent,
664:             reason=reason,
665:             question_key=question,
666:             text=reply_text,
667:             now=now,
668:         )
669: 
670:         await self._uow.commit()
671:         return AnalysisReport(
672:             session_id=session.id,
673:             message_id=message_id,
674:             intent=intent,
675:             confidence=confidence,
676:             used_llm=used_llm,
677:             accepted=accepted,
678:             reason=reason,
679:             facts=facts.as_context() if accepted else {},
680:             rejected_facts=dict(facts.rejected),
681:             next_step=next_step.value if next_step else None,
682:             question_key=question,
683:             cost_usd=cost_usd,
684:         )
685: 
686:     async def _stage_reply(
687:         self,
688:         session: ConversationSession,
689:         *,
690:         intent: str,
691:         reason: str | None,
692:         question_key: str | None,
693:         now: datetime,
694:         text: str | None = None,
695:     ) -> None:
696:         """Request the one reply this turn owes the user.
697: 
698:         Which question comes next is decided above; this only records that an
699:         answer is due and, when the model wrote one, the sentence to send. A
700:         missing ``text`` is not a silent thread: the outbound layer renders the
701:         stable copy for the ``question_key``, which is the deterministic path.
702:         """
703:         self._uow.events.stage(
704:             [
705:                 WhatsAppMessageSendRequested(
706:                     aggregate_type="ConversationSession",
707:                     aggregate_id=session.id,
708:                     aggregate_version=session.revision,
709:                     occurred_at=now,
710:                     session_id=session.id,
711:                     recipient_phone=session.phone.e164,
712:                     reply_kind=_reply_kind(reason=reason, question_key=question_key),
713:                     question_key=question_key,
714:                     intent=intent,
715:                     text=text,
716:                     language=session.language,
717:                 )
718:             ],
719:             correlation_id=current_context().get("correlation_id") or "unknown",
720:         )
721: 
722:     async def _confirm_listing(
723:         self,
724:         session: ConversationSession,
725:         *,
726:         intent: str,
727:         next_step: FlowStep | None,
728:         now: datetime,
729:     ) -> tuple[str | None, FlowStep | None, uuid.UUID | None]:
730:         """Register the listing when the landlord confirms the summary.
731: 
732:         A confirmation only means something at ``CONFIRM_PROPERTY``; anywhere
733:         else it is ordinary small talk and the flow is left untouched. The
734:         property is *not* attached here: attaching bumps the session revision
735:         and would break the optimistic-concurrency baseline ``_advance_session``
736:         captures, so the id is handed to it instead.
737:         """
738:         if (
739:             self._listing is None
740:             or intent != "AFFIRMATIVE"
741:             or session.step is not FlowStep.CONFIRM_PROPERTY
742:         ):
743:             return None, next_step, None
744: 
745:         result = await self._listing.register_from_conversation(
746:             user_id=session.user_id,
747:             facts=dict(session.context),
748:             existing_property_id=session.assigned_property_id,
749:             now=now,
750:         )
751:         if result is None:
752:             return _LISTING_UNSAVED_TEXT, next_step, None
753: 
754:         if result.published:
755:             return None, FlowStep.PUBLISHED, result.property_id
756:         return _missing_listing_reply(result.missing), FlowStep.COLLECT_MEDIA, result.property_id
757: 
758:     async def _advance_session(
759:         self,
760:         session: ConversationSession,
761:         intent: str,
762:         facts: ExtractedFacts,
763:         next_step: FlowStep | None,
764:         *,
765:         now: datetime,
766:         attach_property_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
767:     ) -> None:
768:         """Open the flow if needed, merge the facts, move to the chosen step.
769: 
770:         ``expected_revision`` is the revision read at load time, so if another
771:         worker moved this session meanwhile the save is refused and the analysis
772:         is discarded instead of overwriting a concurrent step.
773:         """
774:         observed = session.revision
775: 
776:         opening_flow = FLOW_BY_OPENING_INTENT.get(intent)
777:         if opening_flow is not None and session.flow is not opening_flow:
778:             # Resets the context, so it must come first: the facts about to be
779:             # merged belong to this new attempt, not to the abandoned one.
780:             session.start_flow(opening_flow, now=now, first_step=next_step or FlowStep.START)
781: 
782:         # Transition before merging: `transition` compares expected_revision
783:         # against the current revision, and merging first would bump it and make
784:         # every save look like a conflict.
785:         if next_step is not None:
786:             session.transition(next_step, now=now, expected_revision=session.revision)
787:         session.merge_context(facts.as_context(), now=now)
788:         # Attaching after the baseline is captured keeps the save's
789:         # expected_revision equal to the value read from the row.
790:         if attach_property_id is not None:
791:             session.attach_property(attach_property_id, now=now)
792:         question = question_key_for(next_step)
793:         if question:
794:             session.context["next_question"] = question
795:         await self._sessions.save(session, expected_revision=observed)
796: 
797:     async def _budget_decision(
798:         self, user_id: uuid.UUID | None, now: datetime
799:     ) -> BudgetDecision:
800:         if self._budget is None:
801:             return BudgetDecision(allowed=True)
802:         today = now.date()
803:         global_spend = await self._usage.total_cost_usd(on=today)
804:         user_spend = (
805:             await self._usage.total_cost_usd(on=today, user_id=user_id)
806:             if user_id is not None
807:             else Decimal("0")
808:         )
809:         return self._budget.evaluate(
810:             global_spend=global_spend,
811:             user_spend=user_spend,
812:             has_user=user_id is not None,
813:         )
814: 
815: 
816: def _reply_kind(*, reason: str | None, question_key: str | None) -> str:
817:     """What kind of answer this turn owes the user.
818: 
819:     Three cases, decided here so the outbound layer never has to re-derive
820:     whether an analysis succeeded. ``reason`` is what the pipeline refused:
821:     answering a question when the message was not understood would move a
822:     conversation the platform never actually followed.
823:     """
824:     if reason is not None:
825:         return "CLARIFY"
826:     return "QUESTION" if question_key else "ACK"
827: 
828: 
829: # The quality gate reports stable codes; the user gets words. Kept here rather
830: # than in the outbound layer because the list is dynamic and cannot be a fixed
831: # ``question_key``.
832: _MISSING_LABELS_FR: dict[str, str] = {
833:     "MISSING_PHOTOS": "des photos",
834:     "MISSING_CHARGES": "les charges mensuelles",
835:     "MISSING_MINIMUM_DURATION": "la durée minimale de location",
836:     "MISSING_AVAILABILITY_DATE": "la date de disponibilité",
837:     "VAGUE_LOCATION": "le quartier précis",
838:     "MISSING_DEPOSIT": "le dépôt de garantie",
839:     "AMBIGUOUS_CONDITIONS": "les conditions de location",
840:     "SUSPICIOUS_PRICE": "le prix, qui semble anormal",
841: }
842: 
843: _LISTING_UNSAVED_TEXT = (
844:     "Je n'ai pas pu enregistrer l'annonce pour le moment. Réessayez dans un instant."
845: )
846: 
847: 
848: def _missing_listing_reply(missing: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
849:     labels = [_MISSING_LABELS_FR.get(code, code) for code in missing]
850:     return (
851:         "C'est enregistré, votre annonce est créée. "
852:         "Pour pouvoir la publier, il manque encore : " + _join_fr(labels) + "."
853:     )
854: 
855: 
856: def _join_fr(items: list[str]) -> str:
857:     if not items:
858:         return "rien"
859:     if len(items) == 1:
860:         return items[0]
861:     return ", ".join(items[:-1]) + " et " + items[-1]
862: 
863: 
864: def build_analysis_prompt(
865:     *,
866:     text: str | None,
867:     language: str,
868:     history: list[TurnSummary],
869:     flow: FlowName,
870:     step: FlowStep,
871:     pending_question: str | None,
872:     known_facts: dict[str, Any],
873: ) -> Prompt:
874:     """Assemble the request, with the state of the conversation as context.
875: 
876:     The context is what turns "Bastos" from noise into an answer: the model can
877:     see that it is replying to the location question of an open listing, and
878:     fill the matching entity instead of guessing an intent from three words.
879: 
880:     The phone number is never part of the prompt: the model has no business
881:     knowing who it is talking to, and prompts end up in vendor logs.
882:     """
883:     return Prompt(
884:         system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
885:         user=json.dumps(
886:             {
887:                 "message": text or "",
888:                 "language": language if language in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES else "fr",
889:                 "you_are_helping": _FLOW_ROLES.get(flow, _FLOW_ROLES[FlowName.SUPPORT]),
890:                 "conversation": {
891:                     "flow": flow.value,
892:                     "step": step.value,
893:                     "awaiting_answer_to": pending_question,
894:                     "known_facts": known_facts,
895:                 },
896:                 # What the form still needs, in order, so the model can both read
897:                 # this message and ask the next question in the same reply.
898:                 "required_fields": _required_fields(flow),
899:                 "price_reference_monthly_xaf": {
900:                     name: {"min": low, "max": high}
901:                     for name, (low, high) in PRICE_REFERENCES_XAF.items()
902:                 },
903:                 "recent_turns": _turns_as_json(history),
904:                 "schema": RESPONSE_SCHEMA,
905:                 "allowed_intents": list(ALLOWED_INTENTS),
906:             },
907:             ensure_ascii=False,
908:         ),
909:         response_schema=RESPONSE_SCHEMA,
910:     )
911: 
912: 
913: def _required_fields(flow: FlowName) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
914:     """The ordered form fields, glossed for the model, in this flow's wording."""
915:     fields: list[dict[str, str]] = []
916:     for name, step in PROPERTY_REQUIREMENTS:
917:         fields.append({"field": name, "ask": question_topic(question_key_for(step), flow) or ""})
918:     return fields
919: 
920: 
921: def build_reply_prompt(
922:     *,
923:     text: str,
924:     language: str,
925:     verdict: _Verdict,
926:     next_key: str | None,
927:     history: list[TurnSummary],
928:     flow: FlowName,
929: ) -> Prompt:
930:     """Ask the model to write the sentence this turn sends back.
931: 
932:     Only accepted facts are shown, and the next question is described in plain
933:     words rather than by its internal key: the model tailors the phrasing, it
934:     does not get to decide what is asked — the code already did. The flow is
935:     passed too, so the wording matches the side of the conversation: a landlord
936:     is asked the rent they *want*, a tenant the rent they *seek*.
937:     """
938:     return Prompt(
939:         system=REPLY_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
940:         user=json.dumps(
941:             {
942:                 "message": text,
943:                 "language": language if language in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES else "fr",
944:                 "you_are_helping": _FLOW_ROLES.get(flow, _FLOW_ROLES[FlowName.SUPPORT]),
945:                 "understood": {
946:                     "intent": verdict.intent,
947:                     "accepted": verdict.accepted,
948:                     "known_facts": verdict.facts.as_context() if verdict.accepted else {},
949:                 },
950:                 # None means "the message was not understood": ask for a rephrase
951:                 # rather than posing a question the platform never reached.
952:                 "ask_about": question_topic(next_key, flow),
953:                 "recent_turns": _turns_as_json(history),
954:             },
955:             ensure_ascii=False,
956:         ),
957:         temperature=0.4,
958:         max_output_tokens=256,
959:     )
960: 
961: 
962: def _turns_as_json(history: list[TurnSummary]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
963:     return [
964:         {
965:             "direction": turn.direction,
966:             "intent": turn.intent,
967:             "confidence": round(turn.confidence, 2),
968:             "used_llm": turn.used_llm,
969:         }
970:         for turn in history
971:     ]

"""Understand one inbound message, with the conversation as context.

The pipeline is deliberately boring:

1. Read the message and its session, then **commit** so no transaction is held
   while a network call runs.
2. Ask the model first, handing it the state of the conversation — the flow, the
   step, the question the user is answering and the facts already known — so a
   bare "Bastos" is understood as an answer and not as noise.
3. Keep a deterministic fast lane for the replies where a model adds nothing: an
   exact "oui"/"non" and a message whose only content is a price.
4. Validate whatever came back through the domain value objects, then write the
   turn, the usage and the session state in one transaction.

The model never decides what happens next: it proposes facts, the code decides
whether they are good enough to move the conversation forward. When a
``ResponseModel`` is configured the same turn also gets a natural-language
reply; otherwise the outbound layer renders a stable template from the key.
"""

display.text:
"""Understand one inbound message, with the conversation as context.

The pipeline is deliberately boring:

1. Read the message and its session, then **commit** so no transaction is held
   while a network call runs.
2. Ask the model first, handing it the state of the conversation — the flow, the
   step, the question the user is answering and the facts already known — so a
   bare "Bastos" is understood as an answer and not as noise.
3. Keep a deterministic fast lane for the replies where a model adds nothing: an
   exact "oui"/"non" and a message whose only content is a price.
4. Validate whatever came back through the domain value objects, then write the
   turn, the usage and the session state in one transaction.

The model never decides what happens next: it proposes facts, the code decides
whether they are good enough to move the conversation forward. When a
``ResponseModel`` is configured the same turn also gets a natural-language
reply; otherwise the outbound layer renders a stable template from the key.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

from loka.bounded_contexts.ai.application.ports import (
    AiUsageLedger,
    BudgetDecision,
    BudgetPolicy,
    ConversationTurn,
    ConversationTurnRepository,
    IntentModel,
    PropertyListing,
    ResponseModel,
    TurnSummary,
    UsageEntry,
)
from loka.bounded_contexts.ai.application.services.deterministic_classifier import (
    DeterministicClassifier,
)
from loka.bounded_contexts.ai.domain.services.ai_provider import LlmUsage, Prompt
from loka.bounded_contexts.ai.domain.services.fact_extraction import (
    FLOW_BY_OPENING_INTENT,
    MIN_ACCEPTED_CONFIDENCE,
    PROPERTY_REQUIREMENTS,
    SUPPORTED_INTENTS,
    ExtractedFacts,
    FactExtractor,
    is_supported_intent,
    question_key_for,
)
from loka.bounded_contexts.messaging.domain.entities.conversation_session import (
    ConversationSession,
    FlowName,
    FlowStep,
)
from loka.bounded_contexts.messaging.domain.events.message_events import (
    WhatsAppMessageSendRequested,
)
from loka.bounded_contexts.messaging.domain.repositories.conversation_session_repository import (
    ConversationSessionRepository,
)
from loka.bounded_contexts.messaging.domain.repositories.inbound_message_repository import (
    InboundMessageRepository,
)
from loka.shared.application.context import current_context
from loka.shared.application.unit_of_work import UnitOfWork
from loka.shared.domain.clock import ensure_utc
from loka.shared.domain.errors import DomainError
from loka.shared.infrastructure.metrics import (
    ai_bypass_total,
    llm_calls_total,
    llm_cost_usd_total,
    llm_latency_seconds,
    llm_tokens_total,
)

USE_CASE = "analyse_conversation_message"
SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES = frozenset({"fr", "en"})

SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You classify WhatsApp messages for a Cameroonian real-estate platform. "
    "Reply with one JSON object and nothing else. "
    "Never invent a value that is not in the message: use null when unsure. "
    "Amounts are in XAF. Numbers must be plain integers."
    " You are given the state of the conversation (flow, step, the question the "
    "user is answering, the facts already known, the ordered required_fields, and "
    "the typical price_reference_monthly_xaf). Use them: a short reply like a "
    "neighbourhood or a number is an answer to that question, so set the matching "
    "entity instead of asking again."
    " A bare number given as a rent is in FCFA: '50' means 50000, not 50."
    " Set 'intent' to exactly one value from 'allowed_intents' and nothing else. "
    "A greeting or small talk is SUPPORT; use UNKNOWN only when no listed intent "
    "applies at all."
    " Also set 'reply': the next WhatsApp message to send, in the conversation's "
    "language, one to three short sentences of plain text (no markdown, no emoji, "
    "no signature). Acknowledge the message briefly, then ask for the first field "
    "in 'required_fields' that is not already in known_facts; if none is missing, "
    "confirm the summary. If the message was not understood, ask the user to "
    "rephrase instead of posing a question."
)

# The closed set the model may choose from. Exposed in the prompt so the model
# never invents a state the platform does not have: an unsupported intent is
# discarded as untrusted, which would turn a simple "bonjour" into a confusing
# rephrase request.
ALLOWED_INTENTS: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(sorted(SUPPORTED_INTENTS))

REPLY_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are Loka, a warm WhatsApp assistant for a Cameroonian real-estate "
    "platform. Write the next message the assistant sends to the user. "
    "Answer in the conversation's language. One to three short sentences, plain "
    "text: no markdown, no emoji, no letter salutation and no signature. "
    "If a question is given, ask it naturally in your own words. "
    "Never invent a listing, a price or a fact that is not in the context, and "
    "never promise anything the platform did not confirm."
)

# A short, provider-neutral gloss for each question, so the reply model knows
# what it is asking for without reading the outbound layer's copy.
QUESTION_TOPICS: dict[str, str] = {
    "ask.property_type": "the type of property (apartment, studio, house, ...)",
    "ask.standing": "whether the property is modern or not",
    "ask.location": "the city and neighbourhood",
    "ask.rent": "the monthly rent, in XAF",
    "ask.features": "the number of bedrooms and bathrooms, and the surface in m2",
    "ask.charges": "whether charges are included and, if not, their monthly amount",
    "ask.minimum_duration": "the minimum rental duration",
    "ask.availability": "whether the property is still available",
    "ask.conditions": "the tenant conditions (deposit, duration, tenant type)",
    "ask.confirm_property": "confirmation of the summary before publishing",
    "confirm.published": "confirmation that the property has been published",
}

# What a month of rent costs here, by property type, in XAF. A model with no
# Cameroonian grounding reads a bare "50" as fifty francs; these wide bands anchor
# the magnitude only — they never reject a price the user is sure about.
PRICE_REFERENCES_XAF: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {
    "ROOM": (10_000, 60_000),
    "STUDIO": (20_000, 150_000),
    "APARTMENT": (40_000, 400_000),
    "HOUSE": (80_000, 800_000),
    "DUPLEX": (150_000, 1_500_000),
}

# The same question is asked from opposite sides: a landlord lists a property, a
# tenant looks for one. The neutral gloss lets the model default to the tenant
# reading ("le loyer que vous recherchez") even in a listing, which reads as if
# the platform had mixed the two roles up. These overlays fix the wording.
_LANDLORD_TOPICS: dict[str, str] = {
    "ask.property_type": "the type of property the landlord is listing",
    "ask.standing": "whether the property the landlord is listing is modern or not",
    "ask.location": "the city and neighbourhood where the property is",
    "ask.rent": "the monthly rent the landlord is asking, in XAF",
}
_TENANT_TOPICS: dict[str, str] = {
    "ask.property_type": "the type of property the tenant is looking for",
    "ask.standing": "whether the tenant wants a modern property or not",
    "ask.location": "the city and neighbourhood the tenant wants",
    "ask.rent": "the maximum monthly rent the tenant is willing to pay, in XAF",
}
_FLOW_TOPICS: dict[FlowName, dict[str, str]] = {
    FlowName.PROPERTY_CREATION: _LANDLORD_TOPICS,
    FlowName.PROPERTY_SEARCH: _TENANT_TOPICS,
}
_FLOW_ROLES: dict[FlowName, str] = {
    FlowName.PROPERTY_CREATION: "a landlord listing a property for rent",
    FlowName.PROPERTY_SEARCH: "a tenant looking for a property to rent",
    FlowName.SUPPORT: "a user who needs help with the platform",
}


def question_topic(next_key: str | None, flow: FlowName) -> str | None:
    """The plain-words gloss of the next question, phrased for this flow."""
    if not next_key:
        return None
    overlay = _FLOW_TOPICS.get(flow, {})
    return overlay.get(next_key) or QUESTION_TOPICS.get(next_key)

RESPONSE_SCHEMA: dict[str, Any] = {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["intent", "confidence", "entities"],
    "properties": {
        "intent": {"type": "string", "enum": list(ALLOWED_INTENTS)},
        "confidence": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1},
        "language": {"type": "string"},
        "reply": {"type": "string"},
        "entities": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "property_type": {"type": "string"},
                "standing": {"type": "string", "enum": ["MODERN", "NON_MODERN"]},
                "city": {"type": "string"},
                "neighbourhood": {"type": "string"},
                "price": {"type": "integer"},
                "bedrooms": {"type": "integer"},
                "bathrooms": {"type": "integer"},
                "surface_area": {"type": "integer"},
            },
        },
    },
}


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AnalysisCommand:
    message_id: uuid.UUID
    session_id: uuid.UUID


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AnalysisReport:
    """What the pipeline concluded, for logs, metrics and the caller."""

    session_id: uuid.UUID
    message_id: uuid.UUID
    intent: str
    confidence: float
    used_llm: bool
    accepted: bool
    reason: str | None
    facts: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    rejected_facts: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    next_step: str | None = None
    question_key: str | None = None
    cost_usd: Decimal = Decimal("0")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class _Verdict:
    """What the domain accepted from one proposed intent."""

    intent: str
    facts: ExtractedFacts
    accepted: bool
    reason: str | None
    next_step: FlowStep | None


class AnalyseConversationMessageUseCase:
    name = USE_CASE

    def __init__(
        self,
        uow: UnitOfWork,
        *,
        inbound: InboundMessageRepository,
        sessions: ConversationSessionRepository,
        turns: ConversationTurnRepository,
        usage: AiUsageLedger,
        classifier: DeterministicClassifier | None = None,
        model: IntentModel | None = None,
        response_model: ResponseModel | None = None,
        extractor: FactExtractor | None = None,
        budget: BudgetPolicy | None = None,
        provider_name: str = "openrouter",
        listing: PropertyListing | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._uow = uow
        self._inbound = inbound
        self._sessions = sessions
        self._turns = turns
        self._usage = usage
        self._classifier = classifier or DeterministicClassifier()
        self._model = model
        self._response_model = response_model
        self._extractor = extractor or FactExtractor()
        self._budget = budget
        self._provider = provider_name
        self._listing = listing

    async def execute(self, command: AnalysisCommand, *, now: datetime) -> AnalysisReport:
        moment = ensure_utc(now)

        message = await self._inbound.get_by_id(command.message_id)
        session = (
            await self._sessions.get_by_id(command.session_id) if message is not None else None
        )
        if message is None or session is None:
            # Nothing was written yet, and inventing a session would be worse
            # than admitting the message is gone.
            return AnalysisReport(
                session_id=command.session_id,
                message_id=command.message_id,
                intent="UNKNOWN",
                confidence=0.0,
                used_llm=False,
                accepted=False,
                reason="message_not_found" if message is None else "session_not_found",
            )

        history = await self._turns.recent(session.id, limit=5)

        # Nothing has been written yet, so releasing the transaction costs
        # nothing and the model call never holds a database connection.
        await self._uow.commit()

        text = message.text or ""
        pending = session.context.get("next_question")
        pending_key = pending if isinstance(pending, str) else None

        if self._model is None:
            return await self._without_a_model(
                session,
                message_id=command.message_id,
                text=text,
                pending=pending_key,
                now=moment,
            )

        # The rules are a fast lane now, not the primary reader: only replies a
        # model could not improve ("oui", "250 000 fcfa") skip the call. The open
        # question is passed along so a bare "non" answers "moderne ou non"
        # instead of being read as a refusal.
        shortcut = self._classifier.shortcut(text, pending=pending_key)
        if shortcut is not None:
            ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="regex").inc()
            return await self._finish(
                session=session,
                message_id=command.message_id,
                intent=shortcut.intent,
                confidence=shortcut.confidence,
                entities=dict(shortcut.entities),
                used_llm=False,
                latency_ms=0,
                cost_usd=Decimal("0"),
                now=moment,
            )

        decision = await self._budget_decision(session.user_id, moment)
        if not decision.allowed:
            ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="budget").inc()
            return await self._finish(
                session=session,
                message_id=command.message_id,
                intent="UNKNOWN",
                confidence=0.0,
                entities={},
                used_llm=False,
                latency_ms=0,
                cost_usd=Decimal("0"),
                now=moment,
                reason=decision.reason,
            )

        ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="llm").inc()
        prompt = build_analysis_prompt(
            text=message.text,
            language=session.language,
            history=history,
            flow=session.flow,
            step=session.step,
            pending_question=pending_key,
            known_facts=dict(session.context),
        )
        result = await self._model.understand_intent(prompt)
        entities = dict(result.entities)
        # The locale shorthand ("50 mil") is a rule, not a guess: when the
        # message spells one it overrides whatever number the model proposed,
        # because the model's prior reads "mil" as a million.
        shorthand = self._classifier.shorthand_amount(text)
        if shorthand is not None:
            entities["price"] = shorthand
        verdict = self._verdict(
            session=session,
            intent=result.intent,
            confidence=result.confidence,
            entities=entities,
            reason=None,
        )

        # The reply is written before the write transaction opens: an LLM call
        # must never hold a database connection, and a reply that fails degrades
        # to a template rather than to silence.

        # Preferred path: the classification call already wrote the reply in its
        # JSON, so the whole turn costs one round-trip. Only a model that left
        # ``reply`` empty pays for a second call; a deployment that never asks
        # for an inline reply degrades to the same behaviour as before.
        reply_text: str | None = result.reply
        reply_usage: LlmUsage | None = None
        if reply_text is None:
            reply_text, reply_usage = await self._compose_reply(
                verdict=verdict,
                text=text,
                session=session,
                history=history,
                now=moment,
            )

        # Both calls are one turn: the ledger records their sum, so reply traffic
        # cannot spend past a budget that only counted intent calls.
        call_usage = result.usage
        model_name = call_usage.model if call_usage is not None else self._model.model
        input_tokens = call_usage.input_tokens if call_usage is not None else 0
        output_tokens = call_usage.output_tokens if call_usage is not None else 0
        latency_ms = call_usage.latency_ms if call_usage is not None else 0
        cost_usd = (
            Decimal(str(call_usage.estimated_cost_usd))
            if call_usage is not None
            else Decimal("0")
        )
        if reply_usage is not None:
            input_tokens += reply_usage.input_tokens
            output_tokens += reply_usage.output_tokens
            latency_ms += reply_usage.latency_ms
            cost_usd += Decimal(str(reply_usage.estimated_cost_usd))

        llm_calls_total.labels(use_case=USE_CASE, model=model_name, outcome="ok").inc()
        llm_tokens_total.labels(model=model_name, direction="input").inc(input_tokens)
        llm_tokens_total.labels(model=model_name, direction="output").inc(output_tokens)
        llm_latency_seconds.labels(use_case=USE_CASE, model=model_name).observe(
            latency_ms / 1000
        )
        if cost_usd > 0:
            llm_cost_usd_total.labels(use_case=USE_CASE).inc(float(cost_usd))

        return await self._apply(
            session=session,
            message_id=command.message_id,
            verdict=verdict,
            confidence=result.confidence,
            used_llm=True,
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
            cost_usd=cost_usd,
            now=moment,
            model_name=model_name,
            input_tokens=input_tokens,
            output_tokens=output_tokens,
            reply_text=reply_text,
        )

    async def _without_a_model(
        self,
        session: ConversationSession,
        *,
        message_id: uuid.UUID,
        text: str,
        pending: str | None,
        now: datetime,
    ) -> AnalysisReport:
        """The deployment has no AI key: fall back to regexes and templates.

        The rule set here is the full classifier, not the fast lane, because it
        is now the only reader. An unresolved message still records its turn and
        asks the user to rephrase instead of leaving the thread silent.
        """
        match = self._classifier.classify(text, pending=pending)
        if match is not None:
            ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="regex").inc()
            return await self._finish(
                session=session,
                message_id=message_id,
                intent=match.intent,
                confidence=match.confidence,
                entities=dict(match.entities),
                used_llm=False,
                latency_ms=0,
                cost_usd=Decimal("0"),
                now=now,
            )
        ai_bypass_total.labels(stage="budget").inc()
        return await self._finish(
            session=session,
            message_id=message_id,
            intent="UNKNOWN",
            confidence=0.0,
            entities={},
            used_llm=False,
            latency_ms=0,
            cost_usd=Decimal("0"),
            now=now,
            reason="no_model_configured",
        )

    async def _finish(
        self,
        *,
        session: ConversationSession,
        message_id: uuid.UUID,
        intent: str,
        confidence: float,
        entities: dict[str, Any],
        used_llm: bool,
        latency_ms: int,
        cost_usd: Decimal,
        now: datetime,
        reason: str | None = None,
    ) -> AnalysisReport:
        """Close a call that did not reach the model: no reply is written."""
        return await self._apply(
            session=session,
            message_id=message_id,
            verdict=self._verdict(
                session=session,
                intent=intent,
                confidence=confidence,
                entities=entities,
                reason=reason,
            ),
            confidence=confidence,
            used_llm=used_llm,
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
            cost_usd=cost_usd,
            now=now,
        )

    def _verdict(
        self,
        *,
        session: ConversationSession,
        intent: str,
        confidence: float,
        entities: dict[str, Any],
        reason: str | None,
    ) -> _Verdict:
        """Validate a proposal through the domain, before anything is written.

        Split out of ``_apply`` so the reply can be written from the *outcome*
        of the turn — the next question, or the fact it was refused — while the
        write transaction is still closed.
        """
        if not is_supported_intent(intent):
            intent, reason = "UNKNOWN", reason or "unsupported_intent"
        if reason is None and confidence < MIN_ACCEPTED_CONFIDENCE:
            reason = "low_confidence"

        facts = self._extractor.validate(entities)
        # The next step must consider the whole form, not just this message: a
        # landlord who gives their city after naming the property type is one
        # step further, not back at the type question. When this message opens a
        # *new* flow, the old facts belong to the abandoned attempt and are
        # deliberately ignored — matching the reset ``_advance_session`` does.
        opening_flow = FLOW_BY_OPENING_INTENT.get(intent)
        starts_new_flow = opening_flow is not None and session.flow is not opening_flow
        known = {} if starts_new_flow else dict(session.context)
        next_step = (
            self._extractor.next_step(intent, facts, flow=session.flow, known=known)
            if reason is None
            else None
        )
        return _Verdict(
            intent=intent,
            facts=facts,
            accepted=reason is None,
            reason=reason,
            next_step=next_step,
        )

    async def _compose_reply(
        self,
        *,
        verdict: _Verdict,
        text: str,
        session: ConversationSession,
        history: list[TurnSummary],
        now: datetime,
    ) -> tuple[str | None, LlmUsage | None]:
        """Let the model phrase the answer, or return ``(None, None)``.

        ``None`` means "use the template": either no response model is
        configured, or writing it failed. A reply failure must never cost the
        user their turn, so the exception is swallowed here and the outbound
        layer falls back to its stable copy.
        """
        if self._response_model is None or not text.strip():
            return None, None

        next_key = question_key_for(verdict.next_step) if verdict.accepted else None
        prompt = build_reply_prompt(
            text=text,
            language=session.language,
            verdict=verdict,
            next_key=next_key,
            history=history,
            flow=session.flow,
        )
        try:
            response = await self._response_model.generate_response(prompt)
        except DomainError:
            return None, None
        sentence = response.content.strip()
        if not sentence:
            return None, None
        return sentence, response.usage

    async def _apply(
        self,
        *,
        session: ConversationSession,
        message_id: uuid.UUID,
        verdict: _Verdict,
        confidence: float,
        used_llm: bool,
        latency_ms: int,
        cost_usd: Decimal,
        now: datetime,
        model_name: str | None = None,
        input_tokens: int = 0,
        output_tokens: int = 0,
        reply_text: str | None = None,
    ) -> AnalysisReport:
        """Record the turn, move the conversation, and stage the answer.

        Extraction already happened in ``_verdict``; a rejected outcome is still
        recorded, so "the model was unsure" stays measurable instead of being
        silently converted into a wrong listing.
        """
        intent = verdict.intent
        facts = verdict.facts
        next_step = verdict.next_step
        reason = verdict.reason
        accepted = verdict.accepted

        await self._turns.add(
            ConversationTurn(
                session_id=session.id,
                message_id=message_id,
                direction="INBOUND",
                intent=intent,
                confidence=confidence,
                used_llm=used_llm,
                latency_ms=latency_ms,
                occurred_at=now,
            )
        )
        if used_llm:
            await self._usage.append(
                UsageEntry(
                    use_case=USE_CASE,
                    provider=self._provider,
                    model=model_name or "unknown",
                    input_tokens=input_tokens,
                    output_tokens=output_tokens,
                    latency_ms=latency_ms,
                    cost_usd=cost_usd,
                    user_id=session.user_id,
                    conversation_id=session.id,
                    correlation_id=None,
                    occurred_at=now,
                )
            )

        if accepted:
            listing_text, next_step, listing_id = await self._confirm_listing(
                session, intent=intent, next_step=next_step, now=now
            )
            await self._advance_session(
                session, intent, facts, next_step, now=now, attach_property_id=listing_id
            )
            reply_text = listing_text or reply_text

        # Committed with the turn: an analysis the platform understood but never
        # answered is a landlord staring at a silent thread, and no retry can
        # notice a reply that was never staged.
        question = question_key_for(next_step) if accepted else None
        await self._stage_reply(
            session,
            intent=intent,
            reason=reason,
            question_key=question,
            text=reply_text,
            now=now,
        )

        await self._uow.commit()
        return AnalysisReport(
            session_id=session.id,
            message_id=message_id,
            intent=intent,
            confidence=confidence,
            used_llm=used_llm,
            accepted=accepted,
            reason=reason,
            facts=facts.as_context() if accepted else {},
            rejected_facts=dict(facts.rejected),
            next_step=next_step.value if next_step else None,
            question_key=question,
            cost_usd=cost_usd,
        )

    async def _stage_reply(
        self,
        session: ConversationSession,
        *,
        intent: str,
        reason: str | None,
        question_key: str | None,
        now: datetime,
        text: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Request the one reply this turn owes the user.

        Which question comes next is decided above; this only records that an
        answer is due and, when the model wrote one, the sentence to send. A
        missing ``text`` is not a silent thread: the outbound layer renders the
        stable copy for the ``question_key``, which is the deterministic path.
        """
        self._uow.events.stage(
            [
                WhatsAppMessageSendRequested(
                    aggregate_type="ConversationSession",
                    aggregate_id=session.id,
                    aggregate_version=session.revision,
                    occurred_at=now,
                    session_id=session.id,
                    recipient_phone=session.phone.e164,
                    reply_kind=_reply_kind(reason=reason, question_key=question_key),
                    question_key=question_key,
                    intent=intent,
                    text=text,
                    language=session.language,
                )
            ],
            correlation_id=current_context().get("correlation_id") or "unknown",
        )

    async def _confirm_listing(
        self,
        session: ConversationSession,
        *,
        intent: str,
        next_step: FlowStep | None,
        now: datetime,
    ) -> tuple[str | None, FlowStep | None, uuid.UUID | None]:
        """Register the listing when the landlord confirms the summary.

        A confirmation only means something at ``CONFIRM_PROPERTY``; anywhere
        else it is ordinary small talk and the flow is left untouched. The
        property is *not* attached here: attaching bumps the session revision
        and would break the optimistic-concurrency baseline ``_advance_session``
        captures, so the id is handed to it instead.
        """
        if (
            self._listing is None
            or intent != "AFFIRMATIVE"
            or session.step is not FlowStep.CONFIRM_PROPERTY
        ):
            return None, next_step, None

        result = await self._listing.register_from_conversation(
            user_id=session.user_id,
            facts=dict(session.context),
            existing_property_id=session.assigned_property_id,
            now=now,
        )
        if result is None:
            return _LISTING_UNSAVED_TEXT, next_step, None

        if result.published:
            return None, FlowStep.PUBLISHED, result.property_id
        return _missing_listing_reply(result.missing), FlowStep.COLLECT_MEDIA, result.property_id

    async def _advance_session(
        self,
        session: ConversationSession,
        intent: str,
        facts: ExtractedFacts,
        next_step: FlowStep | None,
        *,
        now: datetime,
        attach_property_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Open the flow if needed, merge the facts, move to the chosen step.

        ``expected_revision`` is the revision read at load time, so if another
        worker moved this session meanwhile the save is refused and the analysis
        is discarded instead of overwriting a concurrent step.
        """
        observed = session.revision

        opening_flow = FLOW_BY_OPENING_INTENT.get(intent)
        if opening_flow is not None and session.flow is not opening_flow:
            # Resets the context, so it must come first: the facts about to be
            # merged belong to this new attempt, not to the abandoned one.
            session.start_flow(opening_flow, now=now, first_step=next_step or FlowStep.START)

        # Transition before merging: `transition` compares expected_revision
        # against the current revision, and merging first would bump it and make
        # every save look like a conflict.
        if next_step is not None:
            session.transition(next_step, now=now, expected_revision=session.revision)
        session.merge_context(facts.as_context(), now=now)
        # Attaching after the baseline is captured keeps the save's
        # expected_revision equal to the value read from the row.
        if attach_property_id is not None:
            session.attach_property(attach_property_id, now=now)
        question = question_key_for(next_step)
        if question:
            session.context["next_question"] = question
        await self._sessions.save(session, expected_revision=observed)

    async def _budget_decision(
        self, user_id: uuid.UUID | None, now: datetime
    ) -> BudgetDecision:
        if self._budget is None:
            return BudgetDecision(allowed=True)
        today = now.date()
        global_spend = await self._usage.total_cost_usd(on=today)
        user_spend = (
            await self._usage.total_cost_usd(on=today, user_id=user_id)
            if user_id is not None
            else Decimal("0")
        )
        return self._budget.evaluate(
            global_spend=global_spend,
            user_spend=user_spend,
            has_user=user_id is not None,
        )


def _reply_kind(*, reason: str | None, question_key: str | None) -> str:
    """What kind of answer this turn owes the user.

    Three cases, decided here so the outbound layer never has to re-derive
    whether an analysis succeeded. ``reason`` is what the pipeline refused:
    answering a question when the message was not understood would move a
    conversation the platform never actually followed.
    """
    if reason is not None:
        return "CLARIFY"
    return "QUESTION" if question_key else "ACK"


# The quality gate reports stable codes; the user gets words. Kept here rather
# than in the outbound layer because the list is dynamic and cannot be a fixed
# ``question_key``.
_MISSING_LABELS_FR: dict[str, str] = {
    "MISSING_PHOTOS": "des photos",
    "MISSING_CHARGES": "les charges mensuelles",
    "MISSING_MINIMUM_DURATION": "la durée minimale de location",
    "MISSING_AVAILABILITY_DATE": "la date de disponibilité",
    "VAGUE_LOCATION": "le quartier précis",
    "MISSING_DEPOSIT": "le dépôt de garantie",
    "AMBIGUOUS_CONDITIONS": "les conditions de location",
    "SUSPICIOUS_PRICE": "le prix, qui semble anormal",
}

_LISTING_UNSAVED_TEXT = (
    "Je n'ai pas pu enregistrer l'annonce pour le moment. Réessayez dans un instant."
)


def _missing_listing_reply(missing: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
    labels = [_MISSING_LABELS_FR.get(code, code) for code in missing]
    return (
        "C'est enregistré, votre annonce est créée. "
        "Pour pouvoir la publier, il manque encore : " + _join_fr(labels) + "."
    )


def _join_fr(items: list[str]) -> str:
    if not items:
        return "rien"
    if len(items) == 1:
        return items[0]
    return ", ".join(items[:-1]) + " et " + items[-1]


def build_analysis_prompt(
    *,
    text: str | None,
    language: str,
    history: list[TurnSummary],
    flow: FlowName,
    step: FlowStep,
    pending_question: str | None,
    known_facts: dict[str, Any],
) -> Prompt:
    """Assemble the request, with the state of the conversation as context.

    The context is what turns "Bastos" from noise into an answer: the model can
    see that it is replying to the location question of an open listing, and
    fill the matching entity instead of guessing an intent from three words.

    The phone number is never part of the prompt: the model has no business
    knowing who it is talking to, and prompts end up in vendor logs.
    """
    return Prompt(
        system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        user=json.dumps(
            {
                "message": text or "",
                "language": language if language in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES else "fr",
                "you_are_helping": _FLOW_ROLES.get(flow, _FLOW_ROLES[FlowName.SUPPORT]),
                "conversation": {
                    "flow": flow.value,
                    "step": step.value,
                    "awaiting_answer_to": pending_question,
                    "known_facts": known_facts,
                },
                # What the form still needs, in order, so the model can both read
                # this message and ask the next question in the same reply.
                "required_fields": _required_fields(flow),
                "price_reference_monthly_xaf": {
                    name: {"min": low, "max": high}
                    for name, (low, high) in PRICE_REFERENCES_XAF.items()
                },
                "recent_turns": _turns_as_json(history),
                "schema": RESPONSE_SCHEMA,
                "allowed_intents": list(ALLOWED_INTENTS),
            },
            ensure_ascii=False,
        ),
        response_schema=RESPONSE_SCHEMA,
    )


def _required_fields(flow: FlowName) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """The ordered form fields, glossed for the model, in this flow's wording."""
    fields: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for name, step in PROPERTY_REQUIREMENTS:
        fields.append({"field": name, "ask": question_topic(question_key_for(step), flow) or ""})
    return fields


def build_reply_prompt(
    *,
    text: str,
    language: str,
    verdict: _Verdict,
    next_key: str | None,
    history: list[TurnSummary],
    flow: FlowName,
) -> Prompt:
    """Ask the model to write the sentence this turn sends back.

    Only accepted facts are shown, and the next question is described in plain
    words rather than by its internal key: the model tailors the phrasing, it
    does not get to decide what is asked — the code already did. The flow is
    passed too, so the wording matches the side of the conversation: a landlord
    is asked the rent they *want*, a tenant the rent they *seek*.
    """
    return Prompt(
        system=REPLY_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        user=json.dumps(
            {
                "message": text,
                "language": language if language in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES else "fr",
                "you_are_helping": _FLOW_ROLES.get(flow, _FLOW_ROLES[FlowName.SUPPORT]),
                "understood": {
                    "intent": verdict.intent,
                    "accepted": verdict.accepted,
                    "known_facts": verdict.facts.as_context() if verdict.accepted else {},
                },
                # None means "the message was not understood": ask for a rephrase
                # rather than posing a question the platform never reached.
                "ask_about": question_topic(next_key, flow),
                "recent_turns": _turns_as_json(history),
            },
            ensure_ascii=False,
        ),
        temperature=0.4,
        max_output_tokens=256,
    )


def _turns_as_json(history: list[TurnSummary]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return [
        {
            "direction": turn.direction,
            "intent": turn.intent,
            "confidence": round(turn.confidence, 2),
            "used_llm": turn.used_llm,
        }
        for turn in history
    ]
